iut_type: End Product (smart communication unit with embedded antenna, Bluetooth V4.2 smart module, Seiko Solutions)
customer_question: What exactly does the 'RF 2-item test' (¥200,000) consist of, and is real hardware required for it?
question_variants: What are the specific test items covered under the RF 2-item test quote line?
Do we need an actual physical sample for the RF tests, or can it be done some other way?
actual_issue: Seiko Solutions, planning Bluetooth SIG registration for a communication unit built around a smart module with embedded antenna (Bluetooth V4.2, with LTE/GNSS/WLAN also onboard), asked for clarification on what the quoted 'RF 2-item test' actually covers and whether a physical test sample was required.
plain_english_explanation: The 'RF 2-item test' refers to two specific test items defined in the RF test specification: TP/RCV/CA (receive sensitivity) and TP/TRM/CA (transmit output power). A physical test sample (a modified unit suitable for RF testing) is required to run these tests.
consultant_answer: The RF 2-item test consists of TP/RCV/CA (receive sensitivity) and TP/TRM/CA (transmit output power) as defined in the RF test specification. A test sample (a test-modified actual unit) is required.
decision_logic: RF testing for Bluetooth qualification requires a physical sample because receive sensitivity and transmit power measurements cannot be performed on paper specifications or simulation alone — actual RF performance must be measured.
final_recommendation: When quoting RF test line items, always specify the exact test case IDs (TP/RCV/CA, TP/TRM/CA) and clarify upfront that a physical test sample is mandatory, to avoid back-and-forth clarification later.
risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer assumes no physical hardware is needed and doesn't prepare a test sample in time, the testing schedule will slip.
search_aliases: receive sensitivity transmit power test Bluetooth
